pieces.title: Trace-Inverter-4B-NoBubble
pieces.dek: Problem + final answer → synthetic reasoning trace. No reasoning bubble required.
pieces.summary: The fine-tuned model would randomly fire reasoning, or not fire it at all. I needed a model that could build the missing trace from the problem and final answer alone.

blocks.text: Without a usable reasoning trace, the fine-tuned model did not know what to do with its own thinking. Sometimes it fired. Sometimes it did not. Sometimes it reasoned about an agent having to think instead of actually thinking.
The paper How to Steal Reasoning Without Reasoning Traces proposed learning a synthetic trace from what the target model does expose, rather than needing its hidden chain of thought.

The first is the summary setting: problem, final answer, and a short reasoning summary — what I call the bubble — go into the inversion model. The second is the stricter no-summary setting: the problem and final answer go in without that bubble. The paper trains a separate inversion model for each setting.

With bubble:     I_sum(x, y, b) → t̂
Without bubble:  I_nosum(x, y) → t̂

Jackrong had already built the datasets and a bubble-conditioned Trace Inverter. I trained another Trace-Inverter-4B on the synthetic reasoning, using Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 as the base, and dropped the reasoning summaries from the inputs.
Fair to say, it works like magic.
On the held-out public test, the NoBubble model reached 0.6500 Token F1 and 0.3916 ROUGE-L, against 0.4059 and 0.2081 for the base model. Format pass moved from 0% to 100%.

blocks.caption: Held-out benchmark. Higher Token F1 and ROUGE-L are better; length ratio close to 1.0 is ideal.

images.alt: Qwen3-4B base output showing a format failure
images.caption: Base model: prose in the wrong wrapper.
NoBubble: structured synthetic reasoning from problem + answer.

blocks.text: The paper also compared students trained on the actual reasoning traces against students trained on synthetic inverted traces. In some cases the synthetic traces performed better. The actual traces had backtracking and dead ends; the synthetic traces were cleaner, forward reasoning.
